subject: knight
reasoning:
I'm planning out the module structure for a stylized armored knight, staying within the part, joint, and color limits while mapping out the builder API I'll use for the skeleton and primitives.

I'm sketching the color palette for the armor plates and tabard, keeping flat colors minimal, then starting to plan the actual body parts: helmet, pauldrons, and other armor pieces.

For the joint structure, I'm working out how arms and legs chain together, deciding legs are easiest built as a hip-knee-ankle-toe path with names that leave the last joint as the foot tip.

Now I'm setting specific coordinates: total figure height about 1.9m, hips at 0.95-0.98, knees around 0.5, ankles near 0.1, with thighs roughly 0.46 long and shins 0.42. I'm leaning toward polyline chains for both legs and arms since they give crisp joints rather than smooth curves, and sketching the spine as a path running from the hips up through the chest.

Working through the spine chain naming -- deciding how joints map to path points (each joint sits at the start of its span), and choosing to skip a separate neck joint, instead placing the head joint directly off the last spine joint aimed slightly up and forward. Now starting on the shoulder/arm structure.

Mapping out arm chains mirroring leg chains: each limb uses four points (shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand or hip/knee/ankle/foot) with four names, where the final name becomes the chain's tip joint rather than an extra span. I'm setting up mirroring for left/right sides using a sign multiplier on the x-coordinate, and starting to think about how to attach actual mesh geometry to each joint using a part-and-bone helper.

For limb armor, I'm leaning toward using a sweep function across each chain with a radius and color to create bendable tube-like plates, using rigid skinning so joints stay segmented rather than smoothly blended, which gives a plated armor look rather than a soft tights look.

Approximating the arc-length fractions for thigh, shin, and foot segments to set from/to crop ranges on the chain. I'm keeping the module scoped to around 300-400 lines and planning armor pieces like a lathed great-helm dome and scaled sphere geometries, favoring three.js geometry methods over uncertain builder API options to reduce risk.

For the helmet, I'm defining a lathe profile outline to form the dome shape, positioning it at the head joint with careful height offsets so the total figure height stays proportional to a knight's real-world scale, then adding a dark visor slit box positioned using local offsets relative to the head bone.

For the plume, I'm starting a curved sweep path with a catmull spline beginning at the top of the helmet and curving backward to create a flowing red crest.

Now I'm working on the gorget and breastplate -- considering a torus or cylinder shape for the neck collar attached to the chest bone, and planning a tube sweep along the spine chain for the torso armor.

For the torso shape, I'm using a sweep with a faceted octagonal cross-section and a radius that tapers between waist and chest, giving it an armored, faceted look. I'm also considering adding a trim detail at the chest using a torus shape for extra visual definition.

For the tabard, I'm planning to extrude a cloth-like outline oriented front-facing (using x and y as the plate plane so thickness runs along z), positioning it at the torso front near the waist bone, with the outline shaped like a simple rectangular tabard panel hanging down the chest.

For the emblem, I'm designing a gold Greek cross outline to extrude on top of the tabard, building it as a symmetric plus-shape of points around the center with equal arm widths and lengths, placed slightly forward in z so it sits visibly on the cloth.

I'm reasoning through the depth placement so the tabard, breastplate, and torso don't clip oddly, accepting a small gap since it's meant to hang loosely. Now I'm moving on to the pauldrons, thinking about building the shoulder armor from hemisphere-like sphere geometries stacked at the shoulder joints.

For the arms, I'm sketching out the chain structure with shoulder, elbow, and wrist points bending forward, planning vambrace sweeps with widening radii toward the forearm and gauntlet spheres at the hand tips.

I'm deciding to have the right hand hold a sword pointed upward in a salute-style pose, building the blade as a thin box extending from the fist, with a crossguard and pommel at the grip, parented to the hand joint.

Now I'm adding a heater-shield shape on the left forearm, defining its outline points for a classic pointed-bottom heraldic shield and positioning it angled in front of the body facing forward.

I'm giving it red coloring with a gold cross emblem extruded slightly in front of the shield's surface, rigging the shield to follow the left hand/wrist bone so it moves naturally with the arm.

For the legs, I'm sketching cuisses and greaves as swept shapes along the limb, then sabatons for the feet as boxes positioned between ankle and toe joints, sizing them so the bottom sits just above the floor plane without clipping through it.

Calculating segment lengths for the leg chain to assign parametric t-ranges per bone, then setting taper radii for the thigh and knee cap geometry.

I'm also planning the knee sphere caps (scaled sphere geometry at each knee joint) and thinking through using lathe geometry for the waist faulds, flaring the skirt profile from hip down.

I'll give the lathe four points with 12 segments and no smoothing, which should work fine for the thin skirt shape. For the lamellar plates I'll stylize them as a single lathe piece rather than segmenting radially, then add a torus around the waist for the belt.

Now I'm working on the shoulder pauldrons as dome-shaped sphere hemispheres, placing steel-colored caps at each shoulder joint with slightly varying radii for a layered armor look.

I also need to define the spine sweep path for the torso, running from hips through waist and chest up to the neck, using an elliptical cross-section that widens at the chest for a plate-armor silhouette with octagonal faceting, before figuring out how the hip joints connect in.

Now I'm placing the head joint above the spine chain and sizing the helmet as a lathed shape with a profile that starts narrow at the neck, bulges outward around the mid-helm, then tapers to a rounded crown, leaving a small gap for the gorget piece below it.

For helmet details, I'm adding a dark visor slit box positioned on the front face using model-space coordinates, plus a small gold sphere at the crown to anchor a plume, which I'll sweep along a curved path starting just above the helmet top.

Now I'm working out the sword placement for the right hand, angling a blade box upward from the gripping hand position with a separate cylindrical hilt below it.

Still sizing arm segments...

I'm planning joint naming conventions for the skeleton, using paired names like shoulderL/shoulderR through hand and hip/knee/ankle/foot chains, with the hips as the root joint near the pelvis.

Legs will parent off hips while arms parent off the chest joint at the end of the spine chain, and I'm assigning roles like "spine," "leg," "arm," and "head" to the joints. I'm also setting up the color palette — steel, gold, red, leather, dark tones — while keeping part count well under the limit.

Now I'm sketching the overall file structure: imports for the builder utilities, polyline and catmull helpers for limb and plume paths, and the meta export describing the knight model, then starting to define the steel and other color constants.

I'm defining a cross-shaped outline function for the shield emblem, computing the arm corner coordinates, and then beginning the default export's build function that creates the builder, places the hip joint, and starts the spine chain using a polyline path.

Continuing the build, I'm adding the spine joints for waist, chest, and neck, then setting up the head joint parented to the neck with an upward direction, and now constructing the arm chains for both left and right sides with shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand joints along a polyline.

Setting up arm sweeps and armor pieces...

Still laying out armor pieces...

I'll simplify the radius function to taper the torso smoothly from hip to neck using a sine-based curve, then add a gold trim torus at the waist. I need to make sure the torus's elliptical fit matches the torso's cross-section at that height, so I'm scaling it along the z-axis after rotating it into the correct plane to avoid intersecting the body mesh.

Then I'm positioning a gold buckle box slightly in front of the belt, and sketching out a tabard shape that drapes from the chest down over the hips with a pointed profile, defining its outline points to match the torso's width and depth at each height.

For the emblem, I'm placing a small extruded cross centered on the tabard front, adjusting its thickness so it sits just above the tabard surface without clipping through.

Now moving on to the legs, defining leg bones as a chain with joint positions starting at the hip...

Writing leg rigging code...

Adding the shield emblem and boss positioning, then shaping the shield outline with rounded top corners and a sharp bottom point. For the right arm I'm placing the sword grip, guard, and blade geometry relative to the hand position.

Now I'm setting the blade tip and pommel sphere positions, then building the helmet as a lathed profile with a protruding visor slit box and considering a nasal bar addition.

I'm adding a gold crest ring around the helmet top using a rotated torus, then sketching a catmull-rom plume path sweeping back from the helmet crown for a fan-like red plume. Next I'm placing gauntlet spheres scaled and flattened at the wrist joints.

For hand/foot placement, I decide to use the chain's tip joint, falling back to the last joint in the array if tip is null, and define a small `last()` helper to grab that final joint for both arms and legs. I'm also double-checking that joint and chain names stay unique across the skeleton—waist, chest, neck under spine, hips as root—so parenting resolves correctly without collisions.

Now I'm working out the skirt (faulds) geometry as a lathed profile around the hips, flipping the axis to point downward so the profile coordinates run from 0 to 0.22 instead of using negative y values. I'm sketching the outer and inner wall radii so the band widens from top to bottom, tracing a closed loop through four points that avoids self-intersection.

Checking overlaps: legs pass through the skirt radius fine as armor coverage, the tabard and skirt don't collide since their vertical ranges differ, and the belt torus sits comfortably within the torso bounds at the hips. I'm also verifying overall figure height and ground clearance, confirming the sabaton and skirt bottoms are reasonable, and noting that the shield attaches to the left arm tip while the sword goes on the right, with some parts possibly marked flat for a faceted look.

Starting to write the TypeScript knight build, setting up imports, color palette constants, a cross-section helper, and the builder initialization with the hips joint...

Adding belt, skirt lathe geometry...

The small offset there is fine since the tabard naturally hangs loose. I'm placing a cross emblem centered on the chest, nestled inside the tabard's upper area.

For the helmet, I'm lathing a profile for the helm shape attached to the head bone, but I'm checking the vertical placement against the neck joint and gorget top — there's a gap I need to close, so I'm adjusting the head bone position to tighten the fit, while watching for the helm base radius overlapping the gorget.

I'm adding a visor slit, nasal guard, and gold decorative ring to the helmet, checking each against the lathe profile radius at that height to make sure they sit flush with the surface, then building a feathered plume rising from the back of the helm using a curved sweep.

I'm setting up a symmetric loop to build both arms as joint chains with shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand joints, then sweeping steel segments for the upper and lower arm with rigid skinning, and layering pauldron domes on the shoulders while checking their overlap with the torso and each other.

I'm adding a gauntlet sphere at the hand and considering a wrist cuff, then moving to the legs — building hip-to-foot joint chains, sweeping thigh and shin segments, and placing knee and ankle armor pieces. I'm computing segment lengths and joint parameter positions to make sure the rigid sweep boundaries align correctly with knee and ankle joints, adjusting the thigh and greave end points so the knee sphere bridges any gap, and doing the same length/t-value check for the arm segments to make sure the elbow sphere covers the seam between upper arm and forearm.

For the left hand I'm building a heater-shaped shield using an extruded outline with a sharp bottom point, adding a gold cross emblem and a boss sphere on its face, all parented rigidly to the hand bone. For the right hand I'm assembling a sword from a cylindrical grip, a gold crossguard box, a flat tapered blade, and a pommel sphere, checking that the blade's broad face orientation and position relative to the gauntlet look correct.

Finally I'm running through sanity checks — confirming hips and joint hierarchy, outline typing for the cross and heater shapes, polyline array typing, and torus geometry transforms — before finalizing everything into a single returned rig structure.
